topic.angle: A mental shortcut for how long money takes to double

body.claim: Divide 72 by a yearly growth rate to estimate how many years it takes money to double.
body.why: At 6% a year, 72 ÷ 6 gives 12 years. At 9% it is 8 years. The shortcut works because of how compound growth behaves, and 72 is easy to divide by many rates. It is closest for rates between about 6% and 10%.

probes.question: By the rule of 72, about how long does money take to double at 8% a year?
To estimate years to double, divide ____ by the yearly growth rate in percent.
